notice: Fictional advice and source excerpts for the interface demo. These are not reviewed community recommendations.

advice.text: Tap Pantheon's Q as Darius commits to a last hit, then step back before he can answer with attacks. Chip away at his health over separate trades. Save Pantheon's W for an opening; jumping onto a healthy Darius gives him a chance to extend the fight.
advice.source_excerpt: I would start with spear pokes while he farms and check whether I can leave without taking a return trade. After landing one, I would reset my position. I would want a health lead before using the stun to commit.

advice.text: During Darius's Q windup, Pantheon's W can bring you inside the axe blade. Use that response only if you can leave afterward. If Darius's E is still available and he has a long lane to chase through, walking out of the swing is safer than jumping in.
advice.source_title: Using the stun to avoid the axe blade
advice.source_excerpt: The jump can put you close enough to avoid the damaging outer blade, but you still need an exit. I would check whether his pull is available and how far I am from my turret before choosing to jump toward him.

advice.text: Face Darius with Pantheon's E while backing away from his return damage. The shield does not stop Darius's E from pulling you back. After spending the shield, keep your distance until it returns instead of starting another stun combo without protection.
advice.source_title: Saving the shield for the return trade
advice.source_excerpt: I would keep the shield for his response, facing him as I leave. Blocking damage does not remove the risk of being pulled back. If I have used both the stun and shield, I would wait for those tools before trading again.

advice.text: Farm on your side of the lane when you can, with room to retreat toward your turret. Give up a contested last hit if it puts you in range of Darius's E and a long chase. Stand outside the pull's reach even when you have minions in front of you.
advice.source_title: Choosing which last hits to contest
advice.source_excerpt: I would rather lose one minion than get pulled away from a safe position. A wave near my turret gives me a shorter retreat. Standing behind my minions would not protect me from the pull.

advice.text: Let the bleed stacks from Darius's P expire before you trade again. At five stacks he gains a large attack-damage boost, so another attack can cost more than the last one. If he reaches five stacks, focus on escaping rather than answering with one more hit.
advice.source_excerpt: I would watch my bleed stacks as well as my health bar. Going back in before they expire lets him continue the same fight. At maximum stacks, I would use my escape tools instead of trying to finish a short exchange.

advice.text: Watch the windup of Darius's Q and move beyond the blade if you have space. If you are already next to him, stepping toward the handle avoids the outer hit and its heal. Move away after the swing; staying close lets him follow with Darius's W.
advice.source_title: Avoiding the outer swing and heal
advice.source_excerpt: I would choose my direction before the axe finishes swinging. From a distance I would leave its range; from close up I would aim for the handle. Once the swing ends, I would make room again before his slowing attack.

advice.text: Check Pantheon's P stacks before stepping up and choose which spell you want to empower. Spend the empowerment on Pantheon's Q for poke when you cannot stay in range. Save it for Pantheon's W when you have room to follow the stun with attacks, then plan your next empowered cast.
advice.source_excerpt: I would decide whether I want a poke or a stun-led trade before spending the empowered cast. For a brief opening, I would use the spear. With a safe follow-up, I would consider the stun and attacks, then check my stacks again.

advice.text: Keep enough mana for Pantheon's E when you commit with Pantheon's W. A spear poke costs less than a full combo, so use Pantheon's Q between openings instead of spending your escape budget on repeated all-ins. Back off if you cannot afford the shield afterward.
advice.source_title: Budgeting mana for the way out
advice.source_excerpt: Before jumping in, I would check that I can pay for the shield as well as my damage. I would use spear pokes to conserve mana between larger trades. Having the stun available would not be enough reason to engage if I could not protect the retreat.

advice.text: Push the wave into the enemy turret before looking for a roam with Pantheon's R. Check where your teammates can follow up and leave yourself a route back to lane. If no play develops, return for the next wave instead of waiting out of vision while minions die.
advice.source_title: Preparing the wave before a roam
advice.source_excerpt: I would look at the wave before looking for an ultimate. After pushing it in, I would check for a fight my teammates can reach. If the opening disappears, I would head back rather than keep waiting and lose the next wave.
